title: Mitosis architecture audit and rebuild exploration

completion_criteria.text: Foundational audit of the current engine complete across all four domains: two-layer fan-out, durability/resume, cost/latency, pipeline rigidity + fragility
External research verdict delivered on whether the architecture is correct, with disconfirming pass and cited prior art
The child_process runtime-capability question settled empirically (does dynamic import of node:child_process EXECUTE inside a Workflow script, not merely resolve)

Three open architecture decisions resolved by the user: adopt an off-the-shelf durable-execution runtime vs only its state model; default speculation depth given that rework costs tokens not machine time; which work-type pipelines to define first
An approved architecture spec for the rebuild exists, superseding or explicitly scoping the six paused repair-oriented mitosis threads

spine.active_goal: Implementation HALTED on both tracks by user directive after five fix rounds each introduced a defect on a path its own finding list did not name (0134). Two branches carry real, tested, pushed progress and must NOT be reverted: Track A (fix/hooks-prior-path-self-heal @ 5bc19a4, 692/692) and Track B (feat/workflow-sandbox-harness @ e40a292, 1690/1690). Neither is landed; no PR on either. Next move is a planning pass, not code.
spine.next_step: START HERE IN A FRESH SESSION per user directive: dispatch a dedicated FABLE subagent to understand BOTH tracks and plan a solution so completing either does not regress the other. The plan must state per-track INVARIANTS, not a finding list, and check every step against all of them. Feed it this session's five reproduced escapes as test data - a plan that cannot explain why each would have been caught is not finished. NO CODE until the plan exists. See 0134.
open_risks: CENTRAL LESSON: an implementer given N findings fixes exactly N findings; the N+1th path stays invisible because no artifact says what the system must be true of as a whole. Five rounds proved it. Never dispatch another fix round scoped to a finding list.

Track A round 3 has NEVER BEEN REVIEWED. It deleted the content probe and refactored installer.mjs 426 -> 135 lines into four modules - a big refactor plus behaviour change in one range, the shape that hid the last two escapes. Unverified regardless of 692/692 green.

Track B BLOCKED on a reproduced CRITICAL: createContext({}) leaves a host-realm backing object, so nine bare identifiers (constructor, toString, valueOf, hasOwnProperty, isPrototypeOf, propertyIsEnumerable, toLocaleString, __defineGetter__, __lookupSetter__) bridge to the host.

Track B's host bridge defeats the Date, Math.random and globalThis denials WITHOUT THROWING, and its own suite asserts the one closed route and none of the nine open ones. Reviewer-verified fix: createContext(vm.constants.DONT_CONTEXTIFY).

A false-clean gate is worse than no gate, and this session produced FIVE of them in code written to prevent exactly that. Both artifacts under construction are themselves gates. Green tests have failed to catch a defect five times running - demand reproduced probes.

The deployed plugin cache is an UNVERSIONED HAND-PATCH (0132): installed_plugins.json records 0fe1c02, which lacks the guard, and the file mtime precedes commit 2e91b33 by three minutes. A plugin refresh silently reverts it, restoring a false-clean commit gate.

Track B's compileWorkflow passes dead-export-lint VACUOUSLY - zero real callers, kept alive only by its own TypeError message strings, since tests/ is excluded. Constants VALUE_GLOBALS and ALWAYS_DENIED survive being emptied - unkilled assertions.
Step 1.5 is NOT fundable in isolation - 0116 gates it behind Step 1, which is NOT-LANDED. Stop describing it as the cheapest next move.
MSP-1 stays BLOCKED (0126) until Step 3 lands; Step 3 is the correct SECOND precondition after Step 1. All three section-14 performance claims stay UNMEASURED and 0115's falsifiers unpayable.
Spec anchors are POISON (0128) - every citation was measured against a dirty tree of another branch. Re-derive against the live tree per MSP; never pass the spec's numbers to an implementer.

Every write under .claude/{hooks,rules,lib,workflows} needs per-write human approval - the guard matches lib wholesale, so tests/ is gated too. No unattended fan-out on Track B. Track A is a different repo and is NOT gated.

out_of_scope: Pipelines for refactor, perf, docs or chore - closed by 0118. Limits PIPELINES only, not the PR title type vocabulary.
The feat pipeline - 0110 sequences it second, after the fix pipeline proves the effector boundary and durability model against a machine-checkable oracle.
Speculation depth above 1 - 0109 requires a restack proven for the fix work type first.
Bootstrapping a target repo's test infrastructure as a side effect of shipping - closed by 0117; that is verify-setup, human-invoked.
Adopting an off-the-shelf durable-execution runtime - closed by 0108. A webhook, server or daemon for the relaunch trigger - closed by 0119.
fileScope-only task-edge derivation - rejected by 0116, settled by 0120: edges derive from a deterministic verb driving LSP over a seeded project.
Cluster-aware scheduling, and the journal's 2000-char model-output paging - real defects, but they change the scheduler and step 3 respectively; spec section 1 fences both out.
